scope: Static shipped-artifact output-helper analysis. No application execution, host capture, private frame, source media, face observation or live face coordinates are included.

observations.claim: The CIImage input is constructed from IOSurface or MTLTexture with a one-entry kCIImageColorSpace options dictionary. The provided render body applies only extent scale and translation, with no orientation/flip transform.

0x10002911c forwards the unchanged CIImage and CGRect to CIContext render:toIOSurface:bounds:colorSpace: after nil/empty checks. It does not receive an FxImageTile or imageOrigin and makes no additional image transform.
0x1000291b4 renders BGRA8, RGBAh or RGBAf to a temporary bitmap, then copies rows forward to IOSurface. Both source and destination pointers increment positively; there is no reversed-row copy.

sdk_and_official_samples.observation: FxImageOrigin describes coordinate-axis handedness/direction, Motion bottom-left and FCP top-left. This documentation does not establish IOSurface physical row order.
ioSurface carries image data; imageOrigin is documented as tile origin. No physical row-reversal rule is stated.
Apple FxPlug4 template wraps Metal input/output textures and uses fixed UV vertices, without an imageOrigin branch.
Apple example directly creates CIImage from frame.ioSurface without an origin flip. Its area-average analysis is orientation-invariant, so the example alone cannot establish anatomical direction.

conclusions: The original CI-to-IOSurface direct and bitmap fallback paths contain no additional origin-dependent flip.
Applying FxImageOrigin-based input/output flips is not supported by these original CI paths.
Native host physical storage was not captured. Static facts and controlled IOSurface tests must remain distinct from native Motion/FCP observation.
limitations: Ghidra pseudocode is recovered non-source, not runtime behavior.
This focused check does not assert equivalence of the separate original Metal fragment-shader UV pipeline.
Types and calling conventions are Ghidra decompiler observations, not source declarations.
Register variables, compiler-generated blocks, and pointer arithmetic remain decompiler artifacts.
Pseudocode is neither original source nor guaranteed to compile.

High p-code is decompiler-derived, not original source or runtime behavior. is_dead preserves the Java AST flag; decoded block members can retain that flag, so block_membership separately reports actual syntax-tree membership.
Def-use links do not cross function boundaries and may omit memory aliasing, call side effects, or unresolved indirect flow.
Memory read/write effects include stack and temporary memory operations; they do not identify persistent state or business meaning.
Operation, input, and def-use limits can truncate large functions; inspect truncation, omitted lower bounds, and known omitted counts before drawing conclusions.
Known omitted-edge counts cover links omitted from retained operations; omitted operations may contain additional uncounted links.
Unresolved computed or indirect flows without target addresses are not represented as reference edges.
Thunk and external classifications are Ghidra FunctionManager observations; they do not resolve targetless calls.
Pseudocode and assembly are Ghidra-specific representations, not original source or Hopper-equivalent text.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.
The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
References cover the complete Ghidra function-body AddressSet and exact entry. Dossier incoming edges omit sources owned by that function; procedure_references also retains those internal edges.
The dossier combines Ghidra FunctionManager, Listing, ReferenceManager, BasicBlockModel, and decompiler observations; provider-specific pseudocode and assembly are not cross-provider text invariants.

Resolved reference metadata identifies computed, indirect, external, call, jump, and data edges; unresolved targetless flows remain unknown, and function classifications distinguish thunks and externals.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.
The Java bridge serializes one function request per Program and lets each decompilation run until it completes or the caller cancels.
macOS sessions require a matching executable Ghidra native decompiler; REA checks for it but does not build native components or change Gatekeeper quarantine state.
